flashcards.q: Name the three Log Analytics log tiers and their KQL-capability tradeoff.
flashcards.a: Analytics Logs (~$2.30/GB) support full KQL: joins, summarize, indexing, alerting. Basic Logs (~$0.50/GB) drop joins and summarize entirely -- filter/view only. Auxiliary Logs (~$0.05/GB) target compliance data, queryable only via an async search job, not live KQL.

flashcards.q: State the Log Analytics retention pricing structure.
flashcards.a: 31-day grace period, then Interactive Retention (queryable, up to 2 years) ~$0.10/GB/month, Long-Term Retention (archived, up to 12 years, requires an async search job to query) ~$0.02/GB/month. Workspaces ingesting >100GB/day qualify for commitment-tier discounts.

flashcards.q: What is the single highest-leverage KQL performance discipline?
flashcards.a: Filter with 'where' BEFORE expensive operations like join/summarize. An unfiltered 24-hour query against a high-volume table (e.g. SecurityEvent) can scan 50-500 million rows depending on audit verbosity.

flashcards.q: Compare adaptive sampling and fixed-rate sampling in Application Insights.
flashcards.a: Adaptive sampling (SDK-side, on by default in current SDKs) dynamically adjusts the sampled percentage in real time based on traffic volume. Fixed-rate sampling (SDK-side, manually configured) uses a constant percentage, commonly tuned to 10-25% for steady-state production.

flashcards.q: What happens to a configured ingestion sampling rate when SDK-level sampling is already active?
flashcards.a: It's silently ignored. When the ingestion endpoint detects telemetry already arrived with a sampling rate below 100% (SDK-level adaptive or fixed-rate sampling active), it ignores any configured ingestion sampling rate entirely -- SDK-level sampling takes precedence.

flashcards.q: Estimate daily span-ingestion cost for a service at 100 RPS, 10 spans/request, 100% sampling.
flashcards.a: ~86 million spans/day (100 x 10 x 86,400s). At typical vendor tracing rates of $0.50-2.50 per million spans, that's roughly $43-215/day for ONE moderately-trafficked service running fully unsampled -- the concrete number that makes sampling a cost decision.

flashcards.q: What is Application Insights' current recommended instrumentation approach?
flashcards.a: OpenTelemetry-based instrumentation, replacing the older proprietary Application Insights SDK -- aligning Azure with the same vendor-neutral standard AWS (X-Ray) and GCP (Cloud Trace) have also adopted.

flashcards.q: What is a KQL 'summary rule' and what pattern does it optimize?
flashcards.a: A preview (early 2026) feature that pre-aggregates high-volume raw data at ingestion time into a smaller target table, so recurring queries (detections/dashboards running every few minutes) hit the pre-aggregated table instead of re-scanning raw data -- reported to cut per-query compute by 90%+ for that pattern.

flashcards.q: Compare Azure Cost Management to AWS Cost Explorer.
flashcards.a: Azure Cost Management is generally stronger for organization-wide, cross-subscription budget governance (management-group-scoped budgets mirroring the RBAC hierarchy). AWS Cost Explorer is generally stronger on automated remediation actions and has a longer free historical lookback (12 months).

flashcards.q: Why is KQL described as having no direct AWS/GCP equivalent?
flashcards.a: CloudWatch Logs Insights and Cloud Logging's query languages share surface-level ideas (filtering, aggregation pipelines) but are different engines with different syntax and performance characteristics. KQL is a genuinely distinct, pipe-based skill investment used across Log Analytics, Application Insights, Sentinel, and Fabric's Real-Time Intelligence.

flashcards.q: Log tiers are configured per what unit -- workspace-wide or per-table?
flashcards.a: Per-table (per data source), not workspace-wide -- letting a team route high-volume diagnostic logs to Basic Logs while keeping security events on Analytics Logs, all within a single workspace.
